newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN FRIDAY TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN FRIDAY TRADE.

text.p: Zimbabwe's short-term money rates were quoted mixed in quiet trade in Friday's market, local dealers said.

They said a national budget unveiled by the finance minister on Thursday would not immediately impact the market and that the announcement of a new 15 percent tax on interest earned on treasury bills to be effected from January 1998 would also have little effect.
"The market is not sure yet of the effect (of the tax) because the mechanism (of collection) is not yet clear," said one dealer, adding:
"But at 15 percent, treasury bills will still an attractive investment as compared to the 30 percent charged on NCDs (Negotiable Certificates of Deposit)."
On Friday, the central Reserve Bank auctioned Z$100 million worth of 91-day treasury bills at 24.89 percent to mop up some of the liquidity resulting from maturities amounting to Z$230 million.
The central bank bills were also being sold on the secondary market at 24.80 percent while call money fluctuated between 22 and 23 percent.

NCDs with maturity of 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought unchanged at 26.5 percent but sold easier in a 25 to 25.5 percentage range from 26.25. Bankers acceptances were quoted a touch firmer at 25.75 percent from 25.5 percent (buying) but were softer at 24.75 from 25 percent on the selling side.
